findings.text: onTrimMemory drops every sparkline at TRIM_MEMORY_UI_HIDDEN (20 >= TRIM_RUNNING_CRITICAL 15), which Android delivers on EVERY app switch. The sparkAt 5-minute throttle is already stamped, so charts stay blank for up to 5 minutes after returning. This is TJ's 'charts disappeared when I switched back' report. The doc comment's reasoning ('they ride along with the next quote') went stale in Round 56 when the series moved off the quote path.
findings.note: onTrimMemory now releases nothing below TRIM_MODERATE (60); UI_HIDDEN no longer blanks charts

findings.text: After a spark drop the DB (quotes.spark) still holds the series, but nothing re-reads it on return - the recovery path is a network fetch that the throttle suppresses.

refreshSparklines only unmarks sparkAt when EVERY symbol failed. On a partial failure the symbols that failed stay stamped 'just fetched' and are not retried for a full 5 minutes, so individual charts are intermittently missing - TJ's 'sometimes they don't load'.

refreshSparklines is called at the very end of refresh(), AFTER the 'fetched.isEmpty() -> return@launch' early exit. One failed batch quote pass means the candle series is not refreshed at all that tick, even for symbols whose charts are blank.

MarketData.yahoo() and batchYahoo() return immediately when query1 is in a LOCAL cooldown instead of trying query2. Cooldowns are armed per host, so query1 cooling says nothing about query2 - the chart request is abandoned while a usable host sits unused. Contributes to charts not loading.
